En jebero, el acento primario recae en la primera sílaba de palabras bisilábicas y en la segunda sílaba de palabras con tres o más sílabas; ciertos sufijos provocan modificaciones ... [Rojas-Berscia, Napurí & Wang 2020: 419] Minimal pairs are offered below in phonemic transcriptions, with syllable boundaries indicated by dots and stress by [ˈ]. ... ˈna.ni ‘already’ ... na.ˈɾi ‘it is a joke’ ... ni.ˈto.ton ‘intelligent’ ... [fn. 5, p. 422] We are not marking the primary stress in this word because of its complex morphosyntactic nature. More on this phenomenon can be found in the section on metrical stress.

tone_statements.citation: Hart, George, Helen Hart & Esther Gordon de Powlison. 1976. La fonología del chayahuita. Datos Etno-Lingüísticos 28 (microfiche). Yarinacocha/Lima: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano.
tone_statements.quote: En chayahuita hay 11 consonantes, 4 vocales y 4 covocales. [...] Covocales: duración, aspiración, glotalización, nasalización. [...] Las vocales varían éticamente en tono relativo: /i/ es la más alta, /a/ la más baja, y las otras son intermedias. [...] Hay un leve acento que se ocurre en la primera sílaba de cada tema gramatical (y en clíticos de dos o más sílabas). Un mayor análisis podria comprobar que esto es significativo para la palabra fonológica. [...] Este acento tiene el significado gramatical de énfasis y ocurre en la penúltima sílaba de la palabra que se debe enfatizar.
tone_statements.translation: Chayahuita has 11 consonants, 4 vowels and 4 'co-vowels'. [...] Co-vowels: length, aspiration, glottalization, nasalization. [...] The vowels vary etically [non-contrastively] in relative pitch: /i/ is the highest, /a/ the lowest, and the others are intermediate. [...] There is a slight stress that occurs on the first syllable of each grammatical stem (and on clitics of two or more syllables). Further analysis might show that this is significant for the phonological word. [...] This [strong] accent has the grammatical meaning of emphasis and occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word to be emphasised.
tone_statements.locator: part C p. 1-2 (§1, §1.1), p. 14 (§2.2 Palabra and §2.3); etic pitch glides on vowel clusters p. 10
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

Keywords carry stress marks (p. 53: 'Keywords are offered in phonemic transcription with syllable boundaries indicated by dots and stress by [ˈ]', e.g. ˈpa.nɘn 'hill', ka.ˈna.ɾan 'type of otter', ma.ˈna.pa.ɾa 'ring'), but there is no statement of where stress falls and no stress/prosody subsection anywhere in the table of contents.

sources.note: §3.3.3 Rasgos suprasegmentales (p. 30): 'Los rasgos suprasegmentales en la lengua chayahuita son: la duración, la aspiración, la glotalización y la nasalización', quoting Hart et al. 1976: 3 who treat these four as 'covocales'. Stress/acento is not listed or mentioned; the author explicitly defers a new phonological analysis ('no planeamos dar mayor detalle sobre este aspecto de la lengua').

sources.citation: Hart, Helen L. (1988). Diccionario chayahuita-castellano (Canponanquë nisha nisha nonacaso'). Yarinacocha: Ministerio de Educación and Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. 495 pp.
sources.note: Language is not in the catalog and has no existing statements. Hart 1988 says nothing about where word stress falls; it only describes an emphatic accent (extra voice force + post-vocalic aspiration, written with an acute). Cannot be used as a placement statement. Compare Rojas-Berscia, Napurí & Wang 2020 (JIPA, held by the project in the same folder), which marks primary stress on the first or second syllable of every example word but gives no stress section either.
Nothing on stress; phonology tables sourced from Rojas-Berscia 2019 and Barraza 2005.

sources.citation: Hart, Helen (comp.). 1988 [2nd ed. 2008]. Diccionario chayahuita-castellano (Canponanquë nisha nisha nonacaso'). Serie Lingüística Peruana 29. Lima: Ministerio de Educación / Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. 495 pp.
sources.note: No word-stress rule. p. 13 (Ortografía): 'Se emplea el acento ortográfico para indicar énfasis o intensidad' — the written accent marks emphasis, not lexical stress. p. 290 (Notas gramaticales §10.1.5 El vocativo y el énfasis): emphasis is produced 'con mayor fuerza de voz y agregando a la vocal acentuada un sonido parecido al de la j castellana', written with an acute on the 'sílaba acentuada'. The Guía de pronunciación (p. 14) discusses voicing 'después de la segunda sílaba', nasalisation and syncope but not stress.

tone.quote: Note that this study does not take into account the data of a third Kawapanan language, Mikirá, known through a short wordlist collected by Enrique Stanko Vráz and published in Loukotka (1949: 59–64). The reconstruction of Proto-Kawapanan prosody is not attempted either, since the stress system of Shawi is not sufficiently well described.

sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Shawi; every later description cites it. Its treatment of suprasegmentals ('covocales': length, aspiration, glottalisation, nasalisation) is the place a statement on accent/stress (or its absence) would be made. SIL has digitised the DEL series ( for DEL 7 at sil.org/resources/archives/30014), so a probably exists under an entry number that the bot-blocked search page hides.
